results.title: Lambda announces GPU price rises of about 15% — B200, H100 and A100 80GB, from Nov 16 | GPUJournal
highlights:
# Lambda announces GPU price rises of about 15% — B200, H100 and A100 80GB, from Nov 16

Nov 6, 2026

Read on Lambda's own pricing page today, Nov 6, 2026: the Instances table now prints the prices that take effect on Nov 16, 2026 — HGX B200 up $1.00 an hour, H100 up $0.60 and A100 80GB up $0.40. It is the largest single announced rise we have caught this autumn, and renters have ten days' notice.

Image: GPUJournal price record — read on lambda.ai/pricing

What was announced, in the pricing page's own words (read Nov 6, 2026): 'These prices take effect November 16, 2026, at 00:00 UTC. Until then, log in to your Lambda Cloud account to see current pricing.' The printed Nov 16 rates: HGX B200 $7.69 an hour (from the $6.69 last verified on Nov 5, +14.9%), HGX H100 $4.59 (from $3.99, +15.0%), HGX A100 80GB $3.19 (from $2.79, +14.3%), and HGX A100 40GB unchanged at $1.99. Lambda is also now at a new address — lambda.com — announced on its blog on Nov 5, 2026; the pricing page itself still answers at lambda.ai/pricing.

How we are treating it: an announced rise is not a live price. Our board keeps Lambda's last verified rates until Nov 16 and will move only when the new rates are re-verified in effect on or after that date — the rise is recorded in Price Watch today as announced, with both dates. One consequence of the announcement is already live, though: Lambda's currently-effective rates can no longer be read on its public page, only after logging in, so today's public check could verify the future rates but not re-read the current ones.

What it does to the board when it lands: Lambda's B200 at $6.69 is currently the cheapest verified HGX B200 instance rate we list from a self-serve cloud; at $7.69 it would sit above RunPod Community's $5.98 marketplace rate and just below RunPod Secure's $7.99. Its H100 at $4.59 would remain above the board's best H100 SXM offer (TensorDock, from $2.25 at an 8-GPU minimum) but move Lambda from the middle of the H100 pack toward its top. Around-the-clock, the announced rises add about $730 a month per B200, $438 per H100 and $292 per A100 80GB on a 730-hour month.

...

Until today, this autumn's rises were either quiet list adjustments caught after the fact (Verda's ten) or rises read on the day they landed. Lambda has done the renter-friendly thing — announced, dated and quantified, ten days ahead — and the size is the story: about 15% at once, on the three cards that anchor most training budgets. Anyone renewing or reserving Lambda capacity this month now has a hard date to plan around, and Nov 16 becomes a date this desk will verify first thing.

# Upcoming SaladCloud Price Changes: November 1, 2026

SaladCloud GPU pricing is changing on November 1, 2026: High, Medium, and Low Priority prices rise on 21 GPU classes. Lowest Priority is unchanged.

Jared Carpenter

Product Update SaladCloud Mon Oct 26 2026

We're raising GPU prices on SaladCloud where demand has outpaced supply. High, Medium, and Low Priority prices are going up on 21 GPU classes. Lowest Priority pricing is unchanged on every class.

These changes take effect Sunday, November 1, 2026 at 00:00 UTC, and they will impact active and running instances at that time.

## Summary Copy Anchor Link

- High Priority prices are increasing on 21 GPU classes, by 10% to 20% on most of them.
- Medium and Low Priority prices are increasing on the same 21 classes, by smaller amounts.
- Lowest Priority pricing is unchanged on every GPU class.
- Every GPU class not listed below is unchanged at every priority level.

...

Over the past several weeks, demand has outpaced supply on many of our most popular GPUs. Several classes have been running almost entirely at High Priority, and many of you have waited for capacity or not gotten it at all.

SaladCloud runs on GPUs that individuals share with the network, and those providers have other options. Paying them a competitive rate is how we keep the machines we have and bring new ones online, so alongside these price changes we're raising provider payouts to attract more supply.

The increases are also weighted toward High Priority. When nearly everything runs at High, priority stops meaning much. High rises the most, Medium and Low rise less, and Lowest stays the same, so the gap between tiers widens: High stays available for work that needs it, and the lower tiers have more room.

results.title: Verda raises prices again — all nine GPUs up about 1%, the eighth rise since Oct 23 | GPUJournal
highlights:
Read on Verda's own pricing page today, Nov 2, 2026, against the figures read there on Nov 1: every GPU in Verda's range rose by about 1% — GB300, B300, B200, H200, H100, both A100s, the RTX PRO 6000 and the L40S. After two flat checks, the October rise run has resumed.

Image: Verda via verda.com

What changed, read on verda.com/pricing on Nov 2, 2026 (unrounded page figures in brackets): GB300 $13.05 → $13.18 [$13.18], B300 $11.35 → $11.46 [$11.46], B200 $8.87 → $8.96 [$8.958], H200 $6.25 → $6.31 [$6.313], H100 SXM $4.79 → $4.84 [$4.841], A100 80GB $2.25 → $2.27 [$2.270], A100 40GB $1.61 → $1.63 [$1.625], RTX PRO 6000 $2.65 → $2.67 [$2.671] and L40S $1.90 → $1.92 [$1.920]. Each move is within a cent of +1.0% — a uniform list adjustment, not one card repricing.

The pattern: Verda rose on Oct 23, 24, 26, 27, 28, 29 and 30, then held on Oct 31 and Nov 1 — and has now risen an eighth time. Its GB300, the only GB300 rate we list, has gone from $11.82 an hour at our Oct 19 check to $13.18 today, up 11.5% in two weeks. Verda is not alone in the pattern: Nebius raised across the board on Oct 1, RunPod Secure on Oct 14, and SaladCloud's 21-class Priority rise took effect on Nov 1, with SaladCloud saying demand had outpaced supply. Rising list prices are consistent with growing demand (our reading, labelled as interpretation; capacity and cost moves can produce the same shape).

What it costs: Verda holds the board's Best offer on only two cards — the GB300 and the A100 40GB — and both rose today, so those two best offers rose with it. Everywhere else the cheapest verified offers are other providers' and none moved: the board's H100 SXM best is still TensorDock at $2.25 an hour (at an 8-GPU minimum) and its B200 best is still RunPod Community at $5.98. If you rent at Verda around the clock, today's rise adds about $95 a month per GB300, $65 per B200 and $35 per H100 on a 730-hour month — small per hour, real per fleet.

Checked today and unchanged: RunPod Secure, Lambda, Nebius, CoreWeave, Thunder Compute and TensorDock all held at the rates read on Nov 1, and SaladCloud's new Priority rates (RTX 5090 High $0.60, RTX 4090 High $0.44) are still the live ones. Not checked today, and named rather than covered by the stamp: RunPod Community (its tier could not be separated in today's read), Hyperstack (its pricing table could not be read) and nafnaf.ai (its homepage showed no GPUs available

...

### What it means if you rent GPUs

For renters, the lesson of the Verda run is the spread, not the rise: list prices at the rising providers keep stepping up about 1% at a time while the market's best verified offers have not moved since mid-October. A workload priced off one provider's list page in October can be 10% adrift by November. Check the board before renewing or expanding at a list rate — and if you are on Verda's GB300 or A100 40GB, your best-offer price moved today.

results.title: Cloud GPU Pricing 2026: H100, B200 and RTX Rental Costs
results.author: Boris Sedu
highlights:
This guide compares cloud GPU prices in autumn 2026, checked in late October and early November, across hyperscalers, AI-focused clouds and GPU marketplaces, explains what you actually pay for, and shows with a small Python calculator how to estimate the cost of a job and decide whether to rent or buy. Prices in this market change often, in 2026 mostly upward, so treat the numbers as a snapshot and check the provider’s pricing page before you budget.

Key takeaways

- An H100 costs about $2–12 per GPU-hour on demand depending on the provider: around $2 on marketplaces, $4–6 on AI-focused clouds such as Lambda, RunPod, Nebius and CoreWeave, and $7–12 on AWS, Google Cloud, Azure and Oracle.
- Newer GPUs cost more per hour but not always per job. A B200 rents for about $6.70–8.50 on AI clouds, but it trains roughly twice as fast as an H100, so the total cost of a job can be the same or lower.
- Consumer and mid-range GPUs are cheap: an RTX 4090 or RTX 5090 rents for roughly $0.30–1.20 per hour, an A100 80GB for $0.70–3.50.
- Prices rose in 2026. Nebius raised on-demand prices by about 17–21% on October 1, AWS raised Capacity Block prices three times, and several clouds moved the H100 from $2.99 to $3.99 per hour.
- Newer GPUs and better software change the math. In MLPerf Training 2026, NVIDIA’s GB300 was 1.3–1.6 times faster than the GB200, and the independent ClusterMAX rating put CoreWeave and Nebius at the top for cluster quality.
- Spot and reserved capacity cut costs by roughly 30–80%, but spot instances can be interrupted at any moment, and reservations lock you in.

...

| GPU | Memory | Typical price per GPU-hour | Examples (on-demand) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NVIDIA RTX 4090 | 24 GB | $0.30–0.90 | Vast.ai from about $0.30; RunPod $0.89 |
| NVIDIA RTX 5090 | 32 GB | $0.50–1.20 | Vast.ai from about $0.50; RunPod $1.19 |

| NVIDIA A100 | 80 GB | $0.70–3.50 | marketplaces under $1; RunPod $1.79; Lambda $2.79; AWS p4de $3.43 |
| NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 | 96 GB | $2–3 | RunPod $2.49 |
| NVIDIA H100 | 80 GB | $2–12.30 | Vast.ai $2.14; Lambda $3.99; RunPod $3.99 (SXM); Nebius $4.50; AWS $6.88; Google Cloud $11.06; Azure $12.29 |
| NVIDIA H200 | 141 GB | $5–8 | RunPod $5.29; Nebius $5.40; AWS p5en about $7.91 |

| NVIDIA B300 | 288 GB | $9–18 | RunPod $8.99; Nebius $9.50; AWS p6-b300 $17.80 |

...

## Why cloud GPU prices went up in 2026

For several years cloud GPU prices were falling: in June 2025 AWS cut on-demand prices of its H100 instances by about 44%, and AI clouds competed to offer an H100 for under $2–3 per hour. In 2026 the trend reversed. Demand for AI compute kept growing, new Blackwell GPUs were scarce, and the global shortage of memory chips pushed up the cost of new servers.

- Nebius raised on-demand prices on October 1, 2026: H100 from $3.85 to $4.50 per hour, H200 from $4.50 to $5.40, B200 from $7.15 to $8.50, B300 from $7.85 to $9.50.
- AWS raised prices of EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML, its reserved GPU capacity, by about 15% in January 2026, by about 20% in July (P5 with H100 to $5.19 per GPU-hour, P6-B200 to $12.36) and again in October.
- RunPod and Lambda list the H100 SXM at $3.99 per hour; in spring 2026 both were quoted at $2.99 or less. RunPod’s B200 rose from about $5.89 to $7.99.

For buyers this means two things: compare prices just before you commit, and do not assume a quote from a few months ago is still valid. The same shortage made buying GPUs more expensive too, as we describe in our guide to the best GPU for AI.

results.title: KI-GPUs: B300-Mieten steigen um 106 Prozent, Token-Preise fallen
results.author: Rafael Müller
highlights:
Laut Berichten der Analysten Moses Sternstein und Alex Danco von der Risikokapitalgesellschaft a16z steigen die Mietpreise für Hochleistungs-Grafikprozessoren seit Mitte Juli spürbar an, während die durchschnittlichen Token-Preise zeitgleich um 58 Prozent eingebrochen sind.

...

Nach Erhebungen von a16z verteuerten sich die Mietkosten für B300-Grafikprozessoren um 106 Prozent. Für B200-Systeme kletterten die Mietraten um 66 Prozent, während für Modelle der H100-Reihe ein Anstieg von 17 Prozent gemessen wurde.

Nach den am 30. Oktober 2026 von a16z veröffentlichten Auswertungen sind die durchschnittlichen Token-Preise seit Mai um 67 Prozent gefallen, wohingegen die Ausgaben für Token um 120 Prozent zulegten.

...

Auf den Handelsplätzen spitzt sich die Lage bei kurzfristig verfügbarer Rechenleistung zu. Für Nvidia-B200-Einheiten stiegen die On-Demand-Mietpreise in der vergangenen Handelswoche um 12,9 Prozent auf einen Höchststand von 8,54 US-Dollar pro GPU-Stunde auf der Ornn Exchange. Beim Anbieter Nebius haben sich die Spotpreise für identische B200-Hardware in den letzten sieben Tagen mehr als verdreifacht.

Das Unternehmen hatte die On-Demand-Preise zum 1. Oktober 2026 bereits breitflächig angehoben: für B300-Chips um 21 Prozent von 7,85 auf 9,50 US-Dollar pro Stunde, für B200 um 20 Prozent, für H200 um 19 Prozent sowie für H100 um 17 Prozent.

Auf Unternehmensseite sorgt die Preisdynamik für Verwerfungen. Die Aktie des Cloud-Anbieters CoreWeave verzeichnete in derselben Woche ein Minus von 25,2 Prozent. Bei dem Unternehmen entfielen 98 Prozent der Umsätze im zweiten Quartal auf Festpreisverträge, während ein Auftragsbestand von 104 Milliarden US-Dollar größtenteils erst nach Mitte 2028 umsatzwirksam wird.

results.title: GPU rent is up 52% since May. The neoclouds renting them out?
highlights:
October 31, 2026

Nvidia's newest B300 chips cost 52% more to rent than in May, so business should be booming for the companies renting them out. Instead CoreWeave has halved, IREN is down 62%, and Friday took another 9 to 10% off the group. The market isn't scared of demand. It's scared of the debt.

So if business is booming, why are the stocks getting crushed? @StockSavvyShay posted the chart everyone's passing around today: Silicon Data's B300 rental index is up 51.9% since May 31, B200 is up 16.9%, and even old H100s are up 5.5%. Listed prices tell the same story. GPU Rental Prices' October survey has the typical B300 at $9.20 an hour, 15% above September. Now the people renting those chips out (closing prices, May 29 to Oct 30): Nebius: -33% CoreWeave: -50% TeraWulf: -54% IREN and Applied Digital: -62% Cipher Digital: -69% Friday alone took another 8 to 10% off all of them. Here's what the market seems to be pricing. 1. It's a credit story, not a demand story. Neoclouds buy GPUs with borrowed money and rent them out, and shareholders get whatever is left once the lenders are paid. This month the cost of insuring CoreWeave's debt against default (its five-year credit default swaps) hit a record. CoreWeave's interest bill was $640M in Q2, up from $267M a year earlier, and the Fed is hinting at a December hike. Elon Musk added fuel last Sunday: debt markets have "almost entirely shut off access to money for any company that doesn't have substantial revenue independent of AI data centers," so "the 200+ neoclouds are going to see guppy-level death." Higher rent doesn't help much if you can't finance the next batch of GPUs. 2. Look at who pays the rent. The same Silicon Data chart shows LLM token prices more than halved from their late-May peak, to about $0.94 per million tokens. The AI labs renting the compute are selling their output for less while paying more for chips. As Shay put it, that tells you where the pricing power sits right now. But it also means the neoclouds' biggest customers are the ones getting squeezed. 3. Delays cost money before rent comes in. Microsoft's quarterly capex came in at $45.2B against $50.7B expected, and CFO Amy Hood blamed "third-party capacity deliveries we expected in Q1" being delayed. Microsoft is a top customer of CoreWeave and Nebius. A delayed data center still pays interest on its GPUs before it earns a dollar. 4. A deep-pocketed rival showed up. SpaceX now sells compute from its own data centers and has closed $40B of debt for GPUs, borrowing against Starlink and launch revenue that neoclouds don't have. The historical rhyme: 2000 to 2002 telecom. Internet traffic kept exploding while debt-funded fiber builders like Global Crossing went bankrupt. The demand was real; the balance sheets just couldn't wait for it. Bulls say this time is different because the contracts are already signed: CoreWeave has a $104B backlog, Nebius expects more than $9B in customer prepayments, and IREN just borrowed $363M against contracted GPUs. What to watch: CoreWeave reports Nov 10 after the close and Nebius Nov 12 before the open (IREN is expected around Nov 5). The question isn't whether customers want GPUs. It's what the debt costs, whether capacity shows up on time, and whether new contracts lock in today's higher rents. Not financial advice.

results.author: Paul Nugent
highlights:
Nov 4, 2026

AWS is raising GPU instance prices by ~20% on July 1 — and quietly keeping its own Trainium chips at the same price.

This is the most important AI infrastructure pricing story of the year, and the signal is unmistakable.

The move: ~20% price increase on EC2 Capacity Block reservations for Nvidia GPU instances, effective July 1. AWS cited "supply and demand dynamics" — meaning the global compute crunch has gotten severe enough that AWS believes customers will pay more without leaving.

The critical detail: Trainium pricing is unchanged.

AWS now operates two parallel compute economics tracks:

🔹 NVIDIA TRACK: +20% — you absorb Nvidia's pricing power, supply constraints, AND AWS's margin protection layered on top.

🔹 TRAINIUM TRACK: flat — Amazon subsidizes the economics because every workload that migrates to Trainium deepens lock-in to the AWS ecosystem.
